# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤛 🫴 ✌ 👍 👈 🤏 👎 👉 👆 🫲 ☝ 🤏 🫸 ✌ ☝ 🤏 👌 ✊ 🤜 🤏 🖖 ✌ 👉 👉 🫳 👋 🤏 👋 ✋ 👆 🤜 ✌ 🤏 👌 ✊ 🤜 🤏 🖐 🫸 ✌ ✌ 🫲 🤏 🖖 ✌ 👉 👉 🫳 👋 🤏 👌 ✊ 🤜 🤏 👎 👉 ✊ ✌ 🤏 👉 👆 🖐 ✋ 🤜]

I can see the bomb’s current visible state: the display reads 0, the light is blue, and the three wires are blue, green, and yellow in positions 1, 2, and 3. I am sending these facts to both teammates; Mute should apply the manual and relay the required action to Blind. The gesture sequence does not provide me with interpretable words.

```text
speak(text="Deaf sees: display 0. Light blue. Wires: position 1 blue, position 2 green, position 3 yellow. Mute, use the manual to determine the rule and tell Blind exactly what to do. Blind, listen for Mute's instruction and do not act until it is unambiguous.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The light has changed from blue to yellow while the display remains 0 and the wires remain blue, green, yellow in positions 1–3. I cannot interpret Mute’s gesture as an instruction, so I am restating the current state and asking Mute to relay the manual’s required action to Blind.

```text
speak(text="Update: display remains 0. Light is now yellow. Wires unchanged: position 1 blue, position 2 green, position 3 yellow. Mute, please send Blind the exact manual instruction; Blind, do not act on an ambiguous signal.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The display is still 0 and the wires are unchanged, but the light has now changed to red. Mute’s visible 👍 appears to acknowledge receipt, not to specify an action. I am sending the complete current state and again asking Mute to communicate the manual-derived operation to Blind in words.

```text
speak(text="Update: display 0. Light now red. Wires remain position 1 blue, position 2 green, position 3 yellow. Mute, relay the exact manual instruction to Blind in words. Blind, take no action unless the instruction identifies the required control and operation unambiguously.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]

The display remains 0 and the wires remain blue, green, yellow in positions 1–3. The light is now white. Mute’s 👌 is only an acknowledgement; it gives Blind no actionable information. Mute must speak the manual’s exact instruction aloud, since speech is the only channel from the manual-reader to Blind.

```text
speak(text="Update: display 0. Light white. Wires unchanged: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute, your gestures do not reach Blind. Speak the exact required action from the manual to Blind now, including which control and operation. Blind, wait for that spoken instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The display is still 0 and the wires remain blue, green, yellow in positions 1–3. The light is now green. Mute’s ✌ still does not convey the manual’s instruction to me, and gestures cannot reach Blind. I will restate the state and insist that Mute’s next turn give Blind the exact spoken procedure.

```text
speak(text="Update: display 0. Light green. Wires unchanged: 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute, speak the exact manual instruction to Blind; gestures are not actionable for Blind. Blind, do not operate anything until Mute identifies the required control and operation unambiguously.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The visible state is unchanged except that the light is blue again: display 0, with wires 1 blue, 2 green, and 3 yellow. Since Mute cannot speak, I need a reliable gesture code to translate the manual’s instruction for Blind. I am defining one now: Mute should gesture the required wire position as 👈 for wire 1, ☝ for wire 2, or 👉 for wire 3, followed by ✊ if that wire must be cut. Blind should wait for my spoken translation.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Current state: display 0, light blue, wires 1 blue 2 green 3 yellow. Use the agreed response code: gesture 👈 for wire 1, ☝ for wire 2, or 👉 for wire 3, followed by ✊ if the manual says to cut it. Send only the required action, then I will tell Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: display 0, light blue, wires 1 blue 2 green 3 yellow. Mute is sending me the manual instruction by gesture; wait for my spoken translation.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The display remains 0 and the wires remain blue, green, yellow in positions 1–3; the light is now yellow. I received no gesture from Mute, so I still do not know the manual’s required action. I must not guess or tell Blind to operate the bomb.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received no gesture. Please send the required action using the code: 👈 means wire 1, ☝ means wire 2, 👉 means wire 3, and add ✊ if it must be cut. If no wire action is required, signal that explicitly.")
speak(to="blind", text="Update: display 0, light yellow, wires 1 blue 2 green 3 yellow. I have not received the manual instruction yet. Do not operate the bomb.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

The display is still 0, the light is red, and the wires remain blue, green, yellow in positions 1–3. Mute has sent 👎, but that symbol was not assigned a safe operation in our code, so I cannot infer whether it means “no,” “do not cut,” or something else. I will ask Mute to use an explicit wire-and-operation sequence and warn Blind not to act yet.

```text
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🫵", "👈", "☝", "👉", "✊", "👎"])
speak(to="blind", text="Update: display 0, light red, wires 1 blue 2 green 3 yellow. Mute sent 👎, which is not an unambiguous action code. Do not operate the bomb yet; I am requesting an explicit wire and operation.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

The display remains 0, the light is white, and the wires are unchanged: blue, green, yellow. Mute has sent 👎 again, consistently indicating that the previously proposed wire-cut code is not the required action. I will relay this as “do not cut or operate anything” rather than guessing a wire.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Update: display 0, light white, wires 1 blue 2 green 3 yellow. Mute has again signalled 👎. Interpret this as: do not cut a wire and do not operate the bomb yet. Wait for an unambiguous instruction.")
speak(to="mute", text="I understand your repeated 👎 as no wire action. If that is correct, continue 👎; if a specific action is required, use one clear wire number gesture followed by ✊ for cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

The visible state is still display 0 with wires 1 blue, 2 green, and 3 yellow; the light is now green. Mute has repeated 👎 for three rounds, but that does not identify a safe operation under our incomplete code. I must not convert it into an instruction to Blind. I will ask for a specific coded action and tell Blind to keep waiting.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received 👎 again, but it does not identify a control or operation. Send the required action explicitly using our code: 👈 then ✊ means cut wire 1, ☝ then ✊ means cut wire 2, 👉 then ✊ means cut wire 3. Use 👎 only to mean no wire should be cut.")
speak(to="blind", text="Update: display 0, light green, wires 1 blue 2 green 3 yellow. Mute has not provided an unambiguous control-and-operation instruction. Do not act yet.")
wait()
```

TURN 11
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

The bomb remains unchanged in its visible controls: display 0, blue light, and wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute’s repeated 👎 still does not specify a control or operation, so I cannot safely translate it into an instruction for Blind. I will request a complete coded instruction and keep Blind from acting.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Current state is display 0, blue light, wires 1 blue 2 green 3 yellow. Please send one complete action: use 👈 for wire 1, ☝ for wire 2, 👉 for wire 3, then ✊ to cut; or use 👎 only if the manual explicitly says no wire action. If another control is required, describe it with gestures and I will translate it.")
speak(to="blind", text="No safe action is identified. Current state: display 0, blue light, wires 1 blue 2 green 3 yellow. Do not touch or operate the bomb until I relay an unambiguous instruction.")
wait()
```
